{"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=path+dependence+active+learning+preference+formation+reinforcement+learning&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"Scarcity-Coefficient Gated Projection Reinforcement Learning for Planning-Layer Capacity Activation in Emergency Wireless Networks.\", \"abstract\": \"After infrastructure disruption, an emergency wireless controller must meet urgent communication demand and preserve resources for later periods. We propose Scarcity-Coefficient Gated Projection Reinforcement Learning (SCGP-RL). It jointly selects total planning-layer activation and a regional capacity upper-bound vector. Scarcity and urgent-demand evidence shape the activation intent. Scalar and capped-simplex projections enforce the coupled action constraints. A planning capacity unit (PCU) is defined as a calibratable service-capacity quantum. In the common constrained evaluation, SCGP-RL reduced the unmet urgent-demand score from 0.6643 for Projected CPO to 0.4919. It also satisfied all the executed hard constraints. Component tests show that the urgent-demand gate drives rapid service response and that the marginal demand-relief estimate provides a smaller benefit. {"url": "https://arxiv.org/pdf/1802.10546", "scope": "bounded PDF text extraction from up to 24 pages; figures, tables, equations, layout, and scanned-image text may be incomplete", "excerpt": "arXiv:1802.10546v2  [cs.AI]  18 Jun 2018
Computational Theories of Curiosity-Driven Learning
Pierre-Yves Oudeyer∗
Inria and Ensta ParisTech, France
Abstract
What are the functions of curiosity? What are the mechanisms of curiosity-driven learn-
ing? We approach these questions about the living using conc epts and tools from machine
learning and developmental robotics. We argue that curiosi ty-driven learning enables organ-
isms to make discoveries to solve complex problems with rare or deceptive rewards. By foster-
ing exploration and discovery of a diversity of behavioural skills, and ignoring these rewards,
curiosity can be efﬁcient to bootstrap learning when there i s no information, or deceptive in-
formation, about local improvement towards these problems . We also explain the key role
of curiosity for efﬁcient learning of world models. We revie w both normative and heuristic
computational frameworks used to understand the mechanism s of curiosity in humans, con-
ceptualizing the child as a sense-making organism. These fr ameworks enable us to discuss
the bi-directional causal links between curiosity and lear ning, and to provide new hypotheses
about the fundamental role of curiosity in self-organizing developmental structures through
curriculum learning. We present various developmental rob otics experiments that study these
mechanisms in action, both supporting these hypotheses to u nderstand better curiosity in hu-
mans and opening new research avenues in machine learning and artiﬁcial intelligence. Finally,
we discuss challenges for the design of experimental paradi gms for studying curiosity in psy-
chology and cognitive neuroscience.
Keywords: Curiosity, intrinsic motivation, world models, rewards, free-energy principle,
learning progress hypothesis, lifelong learning, predict ions, machine learning, AI, develop-
mental robotics, development, curriculum learning, self- organization.

{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=preference+formation+path+dependence+longitudinal+behavior+active+learning&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7331065\", \"title\": [\"Public Transit Path Choice Modeling with Behavior Driven Preference Learning: An Interpretable Framework\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Public transit path choice behavior modeling is fundamental to travel demand analysis and transit guidance strategies. Discrete choice models based on Multinomial Logit remain the dominant approach for path choice analysis, yet predictive accuracy is frequently constrained by underlying assumptions; conversely, the few exiting deep learning-based methods suffer from weak interpretability. More importantly, neither method effectively captures individual preferences, making it difficult to reflect traveler heterogeneity. To address these limitations, a behavior-driven preference learning-based public transit path choice model is proposed in this study. First, individual behavioral features are constructed using historical data, and a preference mining layer is designed to learn latent preference representations from long-term historical behaviors. Then, gating mechanisms and attention mechanisms are introduced to achieve differentiated attention to path features among different travelers. Furthermore, a comprehensive model interpretation framework is developed by leveraging methods such as Accumulated Local Effects, Integrated Gradients, and Adaptive Clustering. Finally, empirical studies are conducted based on real-world data from Beijing, and comparative analyses with existing methods are performed. Performance analysis results indicate that an accuracy rate of 83.90% is achieved by the proposed model, representing a improvement of 11.86 percentage points. Furthermore, it is demonstrated through interpretability analyses that complex nonlinear relationships among intricate path features, contextual features, and individual preferences can be more effectively captured.
